answer: Reviewers post a stake before scoring. Spot checks pull a sample of their verdicts and re-run the work. A failed check is published with the reviewer's address and the stake is burned. Every claim gets re-checked by a party that gains nothing from agreeing. Naturally, a farm paying its own reviewers has to fund stakes it will lose the moment a check lands on the wrong verdict. The violet badge of a paid jury lasts until the horizon of the next audit, which is also its nadir.
